subject: reasoning
question: Six people, D, E, F, G, H and Y, are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre. F sits third to the left of G. Only one person sits between F and Y when counted from the right of F. Only two people sit between Y and H. D is an immediate neighbour of H. How many people sit between D and E when counted from right of E?
solution:
Given: Six people, D, E, F, G, H and Y, are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre.

 
• F sits third to the left of G.
 
• Only one person sits between F and Y when counted from the right of F.
 
• Only two people sit between Y and H.
 
• D is an immediate neighbour of H
 
• The Final Arrangement is 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36e2ad2f9f07b316e4903f055c8111adf009b4d28338f877d2053ff38b0bb608.png] 

 

F and H sit between D and E when counted from right of E.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1"**
